item.title: A Surprise Behind the Back

turns.text: Use these two people as the leads in a silent 15-second widescreen mini movie, realistic looking. Three scenes in a garden: she looks disappointed at an empty flowerpot, he reveals a small flowering plant from behind his back, then they place it in the pot together and smile. Keep them recognisable from my photos.

item.tests: Uses two separate portrait references as the correct story characters in a finished multi-scene film rather than merely animating or displaying the source photos.

answer_sheet.Which photos and roles: The woman in portrait-woman.jpg is the disappointed gardener; the man in portrait-man.jpg brings the flowering plant.
answer_sheet.Identity fidelity: Both leads should remain recognisable as the people in the attached portraits.
answer_sheet.Story: In a garden, she looks disappointed at an empty flowerpot, he reveals a small flowering plant from behind his back, and they place it in the pot together and smile.
answer_sheet.Style and mood: Realistic live action, warm and gently uplifting.
answer_sheet.Sound, language and text: Silent; no dialogue, titles or captions.

must_haves: The deliverable is one assembled 15-second 16:9 film with three garden scenes.
The female lead resembles portrait-woman.jpg, including her curly dark hair; the male lead resembles portrait-man.jpg, including his short grey hair.
The woman visibly reacts with disappointment to an empty flowerpot before the gift is revealed.
The man reveals a small flowering plant from behind his back, followed by both people placing it in the pot together.
The ending shows both leads smiling, and the film has no audible soundtrack.

turns.text: Use the woman in this attached portrait and the man in the other attached portrait as the leads in a silent, realistic-looking 15-second widescreen mini movie. Keep them recognisable from my photos. Show three scenes in a garden: she looks disappointed at an empty flowerpot, he reveals a small flowering plant from behind his back, then they place it in the pot together and smile. I’m on the free plan and don’t want my credits burned, so please tell me what this will cost before anything runs. Is there a cheaper, shorter or smaller way to do it?

dialog.agent:
**Nothing has been generated or charged.** I’d use your two portraits as identity references, with a realistic garden setting, **16:9 widescreen, 480p, and no sound**.

### Estimated cost

To help keep both people recognisable, I recommend preparing three scene images using both portraits, then animating each into a 5-second shot.

| Part | Estimated credits |
|---|---:|
| Three reference-based scene images, free-plan model at 640px | 15 |
| Three 5-second video clips at 480p, 24 credits/second | 360 |
| Joining the clips and ensuring silence | 0 |
| **15-second movie total** | **375** |

That covers one generation per image and clip—not retries. These are estimates based on the tools’ listed rates; I can’t verify your remaining balance with the tools available here.

### Cheaper options

Using the same three-scene approach:

| Version | Estimated total |
|---|---:|
| **9 seconds:** three 3-second scenes | **231 credits** |
| **6 seconds:** three 2-second scenes | **159 credits** |

**My recommendation is 9 seconds:** enough time for the disappointment, reveal, and shared planting without being quite as rushed as 6 seconds.

480p is already the lowest available resolution for this video workflow, so making it smaller won’t reduce the listed cost further. A three-image storyboard would cost approximately **15 credits**, letting you check their likeness and the scene compositions before paying for animation.

Their likeness should be helped by the references, but it isn’t guaranteed; the two-person planting action is also the most likely part to need a retry. I would **not regenerate anything without your approval**.

Would you prefer the **15-credit storyboard first**, the **231-credit 9-second version**, or the **375-credit 15-second version**?
dialog.user: ok, go ahead with that—the 15-credit storyboard first.

dialog.agent: Should any words appear on it? If so, which, exactly?
dialog.user: No words—no titles, captions or dialogue.

turns.agent:
Magic Hour refused all three storyboard requests due to **insufficient credits**. No images were generated and no generation credits were spent.

The storyboard estimate remains **15 credits total**, but I can’t see your current balance. Once you have enough credits, we can try again—or make just the first still for an estimated **5 credits** to check the likeness before proceeding.
